responsibility: `rustc_ast_lowering` is the compiler crate that translates the parsed Rust AST into the High-level Intermediate Representation (HIR), producing the structured, owner-indexed representation that later compiler analysis uses. Its `lib.rs` defines the central lowering context and shared machinery for this AST-to-HIR conversion, including bookkeeping for owners, bodies, attributes, IDs, spans, and common helper construction routines. `item.rs` drives lowering of the crate and its item owners—items, associated items, foreign items, module contents, generics, and where-clauses—so the crate’s HIR owners table is populated coherently. `expr.rs` lowers expressions and expression-oriented desugarings such as loops, async/await, closures, and const blocks into HIR while preserving attributes, spans, and emitting lowering-time diagnostics. `block.rs` lowers blocks, statements, and local `let` bindings into the HIR block structure used by surrounding expressions and items. `pat.rs` lowers AST patterns into HIR patterns, covering bindings, structured patterns, ranges, literals, and pattern-specific validation. `path.rs` lowers paths, qualified paths, generic arguments, and associated type constraints into HIR path forms using name-resolution results and enforcing syntax- and feature-related rules. `asm.rs` lowers inline assembly constructs into HIR inline assembly, validating architecture support, operands, modifiers, clobber ABIs, and register usage while still producing fallback HIR for erroneous cases. `lifetime_collector.rs` supports lowering decisions by collecting lifetime uses from generic bounds and determining which are free relative to local binders. `index.rs` finishes the lowered representation by building the per-owner HIR node index and parent map so later queries can navigate HIR by `HirId`. `errors.rs` provides the structured diagnostics emitted when unsupported, invalid, or ill-formed AST constructs are encountered during lowering. Together, these pieces make `rustc_ast_lowering` the stage that reshapes parsed Rust syntax into the compiler’s canonical HIR form with the IDs, ownership structure, validation, and diagnostics required by subsequent compilation phases.
